text.about:
In 2026, the Legislature appropriated $35 million in one-time funds to the Chancellor’s Office to support colleges as they build the capacity to offer, award, and transcribe credit for prior learning (CPL) leading to completion and career attainment. This site details the allocation of funds based on per-program current and potential outcomes in compliance with §78093.2(d), which states:

(d)(1) Upon appropriation by the Legislature for purposes of this article, the chancellor’s office shall allocate designated funds to support implementation of this article at each campus using all of the following goals:
(A) Increasing access to credit for prior learning opportunities equitably for all eligible students.
(B) Increasing completion through credit for prior learning awards.
(C) Advancing career attainment through credit for prior learning.
(D) Supporting credit for prior learning opportunities through the chancellor’s office’s pilot projects, such as the California Mapping Articulated Pathways Initiative.

(d)(2) Each campus shall demonstrate that it has implemented the credit for prior learning initiative established pursuant to this article through the metrics described in paragraph (1) before receiving an allocation of funding for purposes of implementing this article.

The Chancellor’s Office measures outcomes in equivalent FTES based on CPL units and allocates funding to institutions proportionally for each priority at an FTES reimbursement rate. Minimum (base) and maximum (cap) funding ensure sustainable support for every participant. CPL funding relies on data in the MAP platform, which serves as the Chancellor’s Office systemwide CPL infrastructure.

text.x_lede:
Senate Bill 135 (Statutes of 2026, Chapter 79), the 2026 education trailer bill, added Article 9 to the Education Code, sections 78093 through 78093.2, effective July 13, 2026. The article establishes the Credit for Prior Learning Initiative and directs the Chancellor’s Office, upon appropriation by the Legislature, to allocate designated funds to support implementation at each campus using four goals: increasing access to credit for prior learning opportunities equitably for all eligible students, increasing completion through credit for prior learning awards, advancing career attainment through credit for prior learning, and supporting credit for prior learning opportunities through the Chancellor’s Office’s pilot projects, “such as the California Mapping Articulated Pathways Initiative.” Each campus demonstrates its implementation through those metrics (§ 78093.2(d)(2)). This page sets out how the Chancellor’s Office proposes to allocate the 2026-27 one-time appropriation across the 2026-27 and 2027-28 fiscal years under that article, and how an institution’s outcomes determine what it qualifies for.

Most of the one-time appropriation is allocated directly to institutions — all 118 of them, the 115 colleges and the three noncredit-only campuses — in proportion to how much teaching each one does, credit and noncredit together. The rest funds the statewide CPL projects and technology that serve every college, and two Chancellor’s Office posts supporting that work. Every institution’s max award — the most it can qualify for on its outcomes — sits between a base award of {base award} and a cap of {cap} across the two years.

An institution’s CPL outcomes determine what it qualifies for. The Chancellor’s Office measures the prior-learning credit each institution puts on students’ records, from that institution’s own MAP data, against {priority count} priorities. An institution meets the baseline requirements to take part; from that point the funding follows the outcomes.
text.reading:
Awards are reflected as max credit (CE) and noncredit (NC) next to the current (curr) amount, which is based on the current outcomes. The CPL an institution actually posts in MAP counts toward its award — Current Total = cap × (actual ÷ target), capped at 100% (an institution at half its target qualifies for half its cap. The current total is the amount dispersed to the colleges according to the funding timeline). Remaining funding rolls forward.

Note: Noncredit awards are counted when a student originates at the district's or college's noncredit program and is awarded credit for the outcomes of the noncredit program. Example: a student takes an Introduction to Computer Networking noncredit course which prepares the student to take the CompTIA Network+ exam and earn that industry certificate (or the noncredit exam is approved by credit faculty for Credit by Exam mastery). When the student qualifies for that credit, Priority 1 FTES are accrued, and if the credit is transcribed, Priority 2 FTES are accrued.

Senate Bill 135 (Chapter 79), the 2026 education trailer bill, added Article 9 to the Education Code, sections 78093 through 78093.2, effective July 13, 2026. The article establishes the Credit for Prior Learning Initiative and directs the Chancellor’s Office, upon appropriation by the Legislature, to allocate designated funds to support implementation at each campus using four goals: increasing access to credit for prior learning opportunities equitably for all eligible students, increasing completion through credit for prior learning awards, advancing career attainment through credit for prior learning, and supporting credit for prior learning opportunities through the Chancellor’s Office’s pilot projects, such as the California Mapping Articulated Pathways Initiative. Most of the one-time appropriation is allocated directly to institutions — 115 credit colleges and three noncredit-only campuses — in proportion to the 2025-2026 credit and noncredit FTES generated. Every institution’s max award based is between a base award of {base award} and a cap of {cap} for the two year period.

The Chancellor’s Office measures the prior-learning credit each students qualify for and the credit listed on students’ records on MAP, against {priority count} priorities. Once an institution meets the baseline requirements, funding is available based on the outcomes.

The use of CPL funding is at the discretion of each institution, since the outcomes are the primary determinant of effective use. The designated college official (CPL Coordinator or administrative lead) is asked to comment on how the funding was used to support CPL implementation directly on their instance of the dashboard.

text.x_alloc:
The Chancellor’s Office measures an institution’s size in full-time equivalent students, its standard measure of instructional volume, counting credit and noncredit instruction together. Across the {institutions} institutions the combined total is {total FTES} FTES. An institution accounting for two percent of that total begins with two percent of the amount allocated to institutions.

The Chancellor’s Office then makes two adjustments to that proportional figure:

- The base award, {base award}, across the two years. {base award count} institutions’ proportional share fell below that amount and is brought up to it, funded from within the same total.
- The cap, {cap}, across the two years. {cap count} institutions’ proportional share exceeded that amount and is held there. The Chancellor’s Office redirects the difference, {cap redirect}, to the institutions below the cap. An institution held at the cap is assessed against a correspondingly smaller target, so it qualifies at the same rate as every institution above the base award.
text.x_count:
The priorities and their shares are above. This is the arithmetic underneath them.

The Chancellor’s Office measures outcomes in units of credit for prior learning, converted to equivalent FTES on the college’s own calendar: 30 semester units make one FTES, or 45 on a quarter calendar.
text.x_timing:
Two timing settings are in effect. Neither changes the amount an institution can qualify for.

- The full two-year amount is made available in year one. The capacity this work requires — staff time, faculty review of credit recommendations, and local process design — is concentrated at the outset, and withholding half of the allocation until year two would delay it. Funding remaining at the end of year one carries forward. Because the entire allocation is available in year one, the targets shown are the full two-year figures.
- Year two mirrors year one. The two years are held identical so that a change to one is reflected in the other. Disabling the mirror leaves both years as they were, so nothing is overwritten.

text.x_lede_figs: Those two lines account for the whole appropriation. The {to institutions} to institutions is one funding total, shared among all 118 in proportion to combined credit + noncredit size within the base award and the cap. Every award then splits into a credit share and a noncredit share by the institution’s own teaching mix: statewide, {noncredit total} is noncredit, carried within {noncredit awards} college awards and restricted to noncredit outcomes. The remaining {2025-26 remaining} million remaining from 2025-26 is a separate distribution.
text.x_count_base: Because the base award is funded from within the same total, an institution above it qualifies for approximately {effective rate} rather than the full {state rate rounded}, while an institution brought up to the base award reaches its target on considerably less. That is the intended trade: the rate per FTES is not uniform across institutions, and the smallest institutions are the ones it favors.
text.x_lede_range: A few very large institutions raise the average: half of the {institutions} institutions are allocated {median award} or less.
text.x_count_factor: A factor above 1.0 raises the FTES reimbursement rate, so fewer units of prior learning reach the priority’s share, which gives more weight to outcomes the Chancellor’s Office intends to encourage. A factor below 1.0 has the opposite effect. The share sets how much funding stands behind a priority; the factor sets the volume of prior learning that qualifies for it.
text.x_count_target: Each priority’s share is divided by its FTES reimbursement rate to set its target. That rate is the 2026-27 state rate of {state rate} per FTES, multiplied by that priority’s funding factor. {factors}
